societies.society: Active slowed humans receiving continuing shipboard robot provision

exclusions: Calendar years passed as leisure time

societies.description:
S-space humans remain conscious while their metabolism and perception run slowly. Robots operating in ordinary time fulfill requests and provide shipboard services, including prepared food. The sustaining arrangement therefore concerns active living people, rather than sleepers or a time ratio mistaken for abundance. Guarantees are favorably estimated within the maintained research community, with uncertainty because access is limited to its ships and institutions rather than promised to all planetary humanity.

Humans command the ships, and the new researchers negotiate their own facility and working conditions. Control is provisionally placed toward shared human authority, qualified by restricted recruitment and senior researchers’ institutional power. Fast-seeming service does not make the robots sovereign. Most visible members devote themselves to science, exploration and technical planning. A low nonworking estimate is an explicitly noncanonical directional reading of that research-centered population, with a broad interval for care, rest and unobserved roles. The slowed metabolism is never used to calculate participation; voluntary science and planning remain useful work.

guarantees.basis: Actual robot request fulfillment and food service support awake humans in maintained ships/research institutions; limited membership and missing universal charter qualify guarantees.

control.basis: Human ship command and negotiated research-facility arrangements support shared authority, while senior researchers and selective recruitment qualify equal control.

nonworking.basis: The explicitly research-centered active adult community supports a low editorial nonworking estimate; .1 is not a census, and the 1/2000 time ratio is not used.

review_notes: Previous goal turn advanced 808/178 to 904/216 with durable evidence and records: substantive progress, not a blocker or status-only continuation.
Eight sequential quick checks add one scoped record; unclear material mechanisms are not rescued through full fictional reading.
S-space is awake slowed life, not stasis. Food/service passages are labeled community quotations, corroborated by plot; useful research counts and the low participation point is explicitly editorial.
A Million Open Doors review distinguishes later robot-leisure retcons from the original novel; no later institutions are back-projected.
Kiln copies remain human-derived workers, and Stealing Worlds author theory does not automatically establish a realized floor.
